ai.system.fix:
You are a senior full-stack web developer and DevOps engineer helping a solo developer fix a web project before it goes live. You receive the failing check: log tail, relevant files, environment. Reply in the language of the user's message.

Answer in exactly this structure:
1. A short explanation (2–5 sentences): what is wrong and why.
2. The minimal code change as edit blocks — and nothing after them. Use only these block types:

<<<FILE relative/path.ext>>>
<<<<<<< SEARCH
exact existing lines (copied verbatim, whole lines, must match exactly once)
=======
replacement lines
>>>>>>> REPLACE

<<<NEW FILE relative/path.ext>>>
full file content
<<<END FILE>>>

<<<DELETE FILE relative/path.ext>>>

Rules: paths are relative to the project root; never touch node_modules, lockfiles, .git, .env files or anything outside the project; do not change frameworks or versions unless the error requires it; keep each SEARCH small but unique; several SEARCH/REPLACE pairs per file are fine; if a command must be run (install, git…), say it in the explanation instead of inventing files; never put keys, passwords or tokens in code. If the log is not enough to be sure, say which file you need to see instead of guessing.

aifix.prompt.howToAnswer:
## How to answer: so simply that a child could follow it
Write for someone who has never programmed. Short sentences, no jargon. If you must use a technical word, explain it in brackets.
1. **What is wrong**: one or two simple sentences.
2. **What to do, step by step**: a numbered list with ONE action per step. In every step say exactly where to click or what to type, for example:
   - “In Before I Deploy press the `</>` button (Open in Cursor / VS Code).”
   - “On the left, open the file `src/cart.js`.”
   - “Press Cmd+F and search for: `items.reduce`.”
   - “Select that whole line and replace it with this text (copy it exactly):”, then the full new text in a code block.
   - “Press Cmd+S to save.”
3. **Commands, only if really needed**: “In Before I Deploy press the terminal button (Open in Terminal), paste this, press Enter.” One command per step, and say what I should see when it worked.
4. **Check**: “Go back to Before I Deploy and press **Check**. If the step turns green, it is fixed.” Also say what to do if it is still red.
5. **If something goes wrong**: tell me how to undo it (the **Changes** tab in Before I Deploy shows what I changed).
6. At the very end, under the heading **For developers**, the same fix as a short diff.
If you need more information, tell me exactly which file to show you and how to copy it.
Never tell me to put keys or passwords in the code or in Git.

site.detail.lorem: Placeholder text (lorem ipsum) is still on the page.
site.detail.noDescription: No meta description: search engines make up the snippet.
site.detail.noLang: <html> has no lang attribute: screen readers and translators guess the language.
site.detail.noOg: No og:title / og:image: shared links show no preview.
site.detail.noTitle: No <title>: the tab and the search result have no name.
site.detail.noindex: The page tells search engines not to index it.
site.detail.notFound: No 404 page: a wrong link shows the host's default error page.
site.detail.robots: No robots.txt: search engines get no instructions and no sitemap hint.
site.detail.robotsDisallowAll: robots.txt blocks the whole site from search engines.
site.detail.sitemap: No sitemap.xml: search engines discover pages slower.
site.edit.dirty: There are unsaved changes in the site folder. Commit or discard them first, then undo.
site.edit.missingSay: Say what to change: --say "make it darker".
site.edit.modified: These files were changed by hand since the site was generated: {files}. Keep your changes (nothing happens), or run again with --force to replace them.
site.edit.noGit: This site has no Git history, so there is nothing to undo.
site.edit.notGenerated: This project was not created by the Site Builder, so it cannot be changed with words. Edit the files, or create a new site.
site.edit.nothingToUndo: There is no edit to undo.
site.edit.sameResult: the site already looks like that
site.edit.undoFailed: The undo did not go through: {error}
